data.title: Port
data.tagline: A port is a numbered network entry that distinguishes services on the same host.
data.learningOutcome: You can identify the host and port in an address and check the target when two local services run together.
data.description: After `npm run dev`, a page commonly opens at `http://localhost:3000`, while an API on the same machine may listen on 4000. localhost means the current device only; ports keep multiple local services separate.

learning.assumes: You have run a local project in a terminal or seen an address such as localhost:3000.
learning.outcome: You can identify the host and port in an address and check the target when two local services run together.

explanation.title: The host identifies a machine
explanation.text: `localhost` identifies the computer you are using, while a deployed domain identifies a publicly reachable server. It does not identify a particular service by itself.

explanation.title: The port identifies the service
explanation.text: The number after the colon directs the request to that service. If a dev server reports 3001 as occupied or switches to 3002, the browser address must change too.

data.boundary: A port is not a domain name or a deployment switch. `localhost:3000` is reachable only on this computer; a correct port does not make a local project public. A port conflict means two services want the same entry, not necessarily that application code failed.

lessonPractice.title: The terminal says the page is running at `http://localhost:3001`, but you keep opening `localhost:3000` and see an old page. What should you do first?

options.label: Open port 3001 as reported, then identify which local service is still serving the old page on 3000
options.feedback: Correct. localhost is the same device; the port decides which service you reach.

options.label: Keep opening port 3000 and restart the current project until the new page replaces the old one
options.feedback: The current project already reports port 3001. Restarting it does not guarantee that the other service using 3000 disappears.

options.label: Make the page service listen on both 3000 and 3001 so both addresses show the same page
options.feedback: That avoids rather than explains the conflict and may take a port another service uses. First identify which service owns each port.

data.agentPrompt: Run `npm run dev` in the project terminal and show me the complete local address from its output. If port 3000 is occupied, state the final port; then open the page and API addresses separately to confirm they reach the intended services.
